meta.title: The Trees Along the West Wall
meta.skill_frame: Find the main idea: decide what a whole passage is mostly about, not one true detail.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: The load is a stated cost, a measured saving, and an unstated change in how a place is used. Measured FK 5.2-6.5 on the three parts (Flesch-Kincaid, approximate syllable count). The load sits inside the grade 4-5 band and climbs one knob at a time across the rung: clue distance, then competing details, then how far the idea sits from words the passage uses.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for main_idea 4.1, sequence 3. No external work.
source.survey: One knob up again: the first two parts state their points, and the third never says what it adds to the whole, so the central idea must combine a saving with a change in use.
source.avoided: No chain store, no real block, no utility rates.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance, competing details, and distance between the idea and the words.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The grocery on the corner has a west wall of bare block. From two in the afternoon the sun hits it, and by four the wall is too hot to touch. Inside, the cooler along that wall ran all day and still could not hold its temperature. The wall faces the street, and nothing stood between it and the sun. The owner screwed a thermometer to the block and wrote down the reading every hour for a week, because he was not measuring the weather. He was measuring what the sun cost him.
passage.part_2: In the fall he planted six shade trees along the wall. They took water for two summers, which meant carrying a bucket out to them, and they needed nothing after that. Three years on, the canopy reaches the roof, and the wall at four o'clock reads twelve degrees cooler than it did. The cooler along it cycles less, and the electric bill for July fell by a tenth. The owner kept the thermometer where it was and kept writing the reading down.
passage.part_3: The trees changed more than the wall. Delivery drivers began parking in the shade, where they fill out their slips. A bench went in under the third tree, and people waiting for the crosstown bus started using it. The bench had been in the owner's garage for years. He had planned a fence along that wall to keep people from leaning on it, and he dropped the fence. On the hottest afternoons, the strip beside the store is now the coolest place on the block.

items.prompt: Why did the owner write down the temperature every hour?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. He wanted to know what the sun was costing him.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The last two sentences say he was not measuring the weather but what the sun cost him, after the cooler failed to hold temperature.
tutor_only.tell: He wanted to measure what the hot wall cost him in cooling.
help: Read the last two sentences of the part.
The owner is not writing down the weather. What is he measuring?
tutor_only.core_idea: He wanted to measure what the sun was costing him.
accept_ideas: to measure what the sun cost him
to see how hot the wall got
to find out what the heat cost
to measure the cost of the sun

if_they_say.when: the student says he wanted the weather report
if_they_say.ask: The passage says he was not measuring the weather. What was he measuring?

items.prompt: What did the owner find after the trees grew?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The wall and the cooler were cooler, and the July bill fell by a tenth.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The part reports a twelve-degree drop at four o'clock, less cycling in the cooler, and a tenth off the July bill.
tutor_only.tell: The trees cooled the wall by twelve degrees, the cooler ran less, and the July bill fell by a tenth.
help: Find the sentence with the twelve degrees.
Look at what happened to the cooler and the bill.
tutor_only.core_idea: The wall was twelve degrees cooler, the cooler cycled less, and the electric bill fell.
accept_ideas: the electric bill fell by a tenth
the trees cut the cooling cost

if_they_say.when: the student says he found the wall was hotter
if_they_say.ask: Compare the reading with the one from before the trees. Which way did it move?

items.prompt: What is the third part mostly about?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The shade changed how people used the strip, and the owner dropped his fence.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The part reports drivers parking in the shade, a bench in use, and the fence the owner decided not to build.
tutor_only.tell: The third part is about people using the shaded strip, and the owner giving up the fence he had planned.
help: Find what the delivery drivers and the bus riders started doing.
Look at what the owner did with his plan for a fence.
tutor_only.core_idea: The shade turned the strip beside the store into a place people use, so the owner dropped his fence.
accept_ideas: the strip became a place to wait
drivers and riders use the shade

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about a fence the owner built
if_they_say.ask: Check the sentence about the fence. Did he build it?

items.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

tutor_only.confirm: The trees cooled the wall, cut the bill, and made the strip a place people use.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Part one is the problem, part two the measured saving, part three the change in how people use the strip.
tutor_only.tell: Six shade trees cooled a hot wall and cut the store's summer bill. They also made the strip beside it a place people use.
help: Name what each part adds about the trees.
The last part is not about the bill. What is it about?
tutor_only.core_idea: Six shade trees cooled a hot wall, cut the store's cooling cost, and made the strip beside it a place people use.
accept_ideas: trees that cooled a store and changed its front
shade trees saved money and made a place to sit
the trees cooled the store and people started using the shade

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about a fence
if_they_say.ask: The fence is the thing the owner did not build. What did the trees do?

if_they_say.when: the student says it is about saving electricity
if_they_say.ask: Electricity is one part. What does the last part say the shade changed?

items.prompt: One reader says the passage is mostly about saving electricity. What does that idea miss?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. It misses the strip beside the store, which the last part is about.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The bill is one measured result in part two. Part three is about drivers, a bench, a bus stop, and a fence the owner dropped.
tutor_only.tell: It misses what happened outside the store. The shade became a place where people park, sit, and wait.
help: Look at what the last part is about.
The bill appears in one part. How many parts are about the strip?
tutor_only.core_idea: It misses the strip beside the store, which the last part is about.
accept_ideas: it misses what happened outside the store
it leaves out the bench and the people using the shade
the shade changed the street too

if_they_say.when: the student says nothing is missing
if_they_say.ask: Read the last part again. Does it mention the electric bill?
